2607.02467.title: Human Capital, Not Model Benchmarks, Predicts Hybrid Intelligence in Forecasting
2607.02467.paper_summary: Whether pairing people with AI helps or hurts is usually reported as a single average effect. Using a real-money prediction market (Polymarket) as an objective, externally resolved benchmark, this pilot shows that the value of human-AI collaboration depends on a specific, measurable form of human capital. Analyzed at the level of the individual forecaster, hybrid performance is trimodal: most people either deferred to the model (matching it) or used it to rubber-stamp a prior guess (performing worse than the model alone), while a minority engaged in genuine complementary reasoning and reached accuracy matching or even exceeding (i.e., lower error than) the market itself. Collaborative traits (perspective-taking, intellectual humility, and curiosity) rather than raw cognitive ability or model benchmarks, distinguished who reached that mode. The results are preliminary but statistically robust, and motivate a pre-registered replication now in preparation.
2607.02467.paper_summary_zh: 無論將人與人工智慧配對是有助於還是有害，通常報導為單一的平均效果。使用真實貨幣預測市場（Polymarket）作為客觀的、外部解決的基準，這項試點顯示人類與人工智慧合作的價值取決於一種特定的、可測量的人力資本形式。在個別預測者的層面上進行分析，混合表現呈現三模態：大多數人要麼依賴模型（與之匹配），要麼用它來確認先前的猜測（表現不如僅使用模型），而少數人則進行真正的互補推理，達到與市場本身匹配甚至超越（即，低於市場的錯誤） 的準確性。協作特質（視角採取、智力謙遜和好奇心）而非純粹的認知能力或模型基準，區分了誰達到了那種模式。結果是初步的，但在統計上是穩健的，並促使一項已註冊的複製研究正在準備中。
2607.02467.author: Vivienne Ming et.al.
